stories.title: Birbal and the Line
body: One day, Emperor Akbar was in a playful mood. He drew a line on the floor of his court and asked all his ministers, "Can any of you make this line shorter — but without erasing any part of it?"
The ministers scratched their heads. How could a line become shorter without rubbing any of it away? It seemed impossible! One by one, they gave up.
Then Birbal stepped forward with a calm smile. He did not touch the emperor's line at all. Instead, he simply drew a much longer line right next to it.
Everyone looked, and sure enough — next to the new longer line, the emperor's line now looked shorter, even though nothing had been erased!

Akbar clapped with delight. "Wonderful, Birbal! You did not remove anything, yet you made my line smaller." Birbal bowed and said, "Your Majesty, to make something look smaller, we need not destroy it — we only have to build something greater beside it." The whole court smiled at Birbal's wisdom.

quiz.q: What did Akbar draw on the floor?

opts: Drew a longer line beside it

quiz.q: How did the first line look then?

opts: Build something greater instead of destroying

stories.title: The Pot of Wisdom
body: A rich but foolish merchant came to Akbar's court. "Your Majesty," he boasted, "I have heard Birbal is very wise. But I have travelled the world and learned much. Let me test him!"

The merchant handed Birbal an empty pot. "Fill this pot with something, and I must not be able to take it out, pour it out, or empty it in any way. If you can do it, I will accept you are wiser than me."

The court fell silent. What could fill a pot yet never be taken out? Birbal thought for only a moment. He walked to the garden, dug a small hole, and buried the pot deep in the earth, leaving only the rim showing.
Then he poured water into the pot until it overflowed. "There," said Birbal. "The pot is full of water, but since it is buried in the ground, you cannot lift it, pour it, or tip it over to empty it."

The merchant was amazed and bowed his head. "You are indeed the wisest man I have met, Birbal." Akbar laughed heartily, proud of his clever minister. True wisdom, he knew, was not about how far you travel, but how well you think.

quiz.q: What did the merchant give Birbal?

opts: Fill it so nothing can be taken out
Buried the pot and filled it with water
